nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — project instructions
nodes.rationale: Single guidance file for Claude Code; documents the composition-host shape so an agent searches modules/ rather than app/.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Agent-facing environment instructions; identical lerd + Laravel Boost body shared with the Copilot, Junie and Gemini files.

nodes.label: Conformance spec and migration plan
nodes.rationale: Plans the flip to module-repo-first; every decision links to the issue holding its reasoning. The document plans and changes nothing.

nodes.label: Code-level conformance audit
nodes.rationale: Records where the fleet stands against code-level standards; fixes nothing so each finding stays a separate decision taken with the measurement in hand.

nodes.label: Composition host
nodes.rationale: app/ holds exactly five files; search, theming, localization, settings, roles and observability live in 40 liberu-module packages and 4 liberu-theme packages. Before assuming a class lives in app/, search modules/.

nodes.label: module.json manifest
nodes.rationale: Declares provider class, capabilities, required packages and capabilities, default_enabled and Filament plugins — the single source of truth for enablement.

nodes.label: ModuleManagerServiceProvider
nodes.rationale: First entry in bootstrap/providers.php so discovery runs before anything depends on it.

nodes.label: ModuleRegistry::resolve
nodes.rationale: Validates constraints with Semver and returns providers in dependency order; disabling a required module raises DependencyResolutionFailed rather than quietly omitting it.

nodes.label: Installation never implies boot
nodes.rationale: No package declares extra.laravel.providers, so Laravel auto-discovery registers nothing and enablement stays an explicit, separate decision. An architecture rule asserts this stays true.

nodes.label: Manifest default_enabled
nodes.rationale: True for 37 of 40; false for analytics-google, analytics-meta and localization-mymemory, which need third-party credentials so ship installed but off. Adding a module to a composition is therefore installing it — there is no second list to remember.

nodes.label: config/modules.php env overrides
nodes.rationale: Holds only MODULES_ENABLED and MODULES_DISABLED, both empty; disabled beats both. Config stays list-free so it cannot become a second source of truth that drifts.

nodes.label: App\Filament\ModulePlugins
nodes.rationale: Instantiates only the plugins of enabled modules, rejecting duplicate ids and non-Plugin types — the runtime guard that always fires before any static rule could.

nodes.label: App\Support\ThemeColors
nodes.rationale: Maps a theme's colors.primary to a Filament palette (unknown → Amber); panel composition is a host concern, so it moved to app/ when foundation-filament dissolved.

nodes.label: AdminPanelProvider
nodes.rationale: Default panel at /admin, tenant-scoped to the Team model with Shield's SyncShieldTenant as persistent tenant middleware.

nodes.label: AppPanelProvider
nodes.rationale: Panel at /app, deliberately not tenant-scoped and open to any authenticated user.

nodes.label: Dual Filament panels
nodes.rationale: Both append SetLocale and SecurityHeaders to ->middleware([]) because Filament panels do not run the web group.

nodes.label: App\Models\User (host composition model)
nodes.rationale: Implements seven contracts from four packages; role checks query the pivot team-agnostically because Spatie's hasRole() is bound to an active team context that is unset when canAccessPanel() or the Telescope/Pulse gates run.

nodes.label: Tenancy rules that bite
nodes.rationale: A Resource whose model has no team() relationship must override isScopedToTenant(); shield:generate must run inside a team context; filament-shield tenant_model and permission models.team are deliberately null.

nodes.label: Spatie Permission (team-scoped roles)
nodes.rationale: permission.teams => true, so roles carry a team_id and Spatie already isolates roles by team — which is why the authorization presentation module disables Shield's tenant resource scoping.

nodes.label: tests/Architecture/ModuleBoundariesTest
nodes.rationale: Holds 8 whole-graph rules only; a rule a package can check about itself belongs in the testbench, because a host rule could only ever fail in the host, which is not where the fault is.

nodes.label: A rule that cannot fire is not coverage
nodes.rationale: Plugin-id uniqueness and renamed-package rules were dropped because ModulePlugins and ModuleValidationGuard reject those conditions first; each was mutation-tested and the failure came from the runtime guard, not the rule.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/package-testbench
nodes.rationale: Owns PackageTestCase, PackageRoot, three shipped Boundary suites and the shared TestUser, plus Pint and PHPStan and their configs — so a new boundary rule is one testbench release rather than a 44-repository sweep.

nodes.label: Packages are standalone-testable
nodes.rationale: Each package carries require-dev, its own phpunit.xml and a thin caller of the reusable workflows; a test belongs in a package only if it needs nothing from the host.

nodes.label: tests/.gitkeep is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Git does not track an empty directory, so a package with no tests of its own published without tests/ at all and Pest aborted with 'The test directory [tests] does not exist'. 34 packages shipped that way once.

nodes.label: TestUser / UsesTestUser
nodes.rationale: Loads the base users migration and brings RefreshDatabase; it implements none of the fleet's actor contracts because doing so would make the testbench require Horizon, Pulse, Telescope, Jetstream, Socialite and Socialstream in all 44 dev trees.

nodes.label: scripts/fleet
nodes.rationale: Clones, runs, commits and pushes across the package repositories but deliberately stops short of tagging: a push is recoverable, a tag is what Packagist publishes and what ModuleValidator pins the host to, so an unattended bad wave would be 44 revert-tags.

nodes.label: scripts/publish-components (removed)
nodes.rationale: Rsynced the monorepo into the package repositories — the opposite direction to the flip — and was removed once the coverage-ratchet wave proved a fleet-wide change could ship through fleet alone.

nodes.label: Packagist names drop the module- prefix
nodes.rationale: liberusoftware/module-search on GitHub is liberusoftware/search on Packagist.

nodes.label: ModuleValidator
nodes.rationale: Compares each manifest against Composer\InstalledVersions, which is why the fleet must keep a version field that composer validate --strict rejects.

nodes.label: ModuleValidationGuard
nodes.rationale: Fails the boot with 'Composer package is not installed' before any architecture rule body runs.

nodes.label: Theme packages and inheritance
nodes.rationale: base is the shared root and the only theme shipping layouts/app.blade.php, so every public theme renders through the fallback.

nodes.label: ThemeManager::inheritanceChain
nodes.rationale: Walks the parent chain with a cycle guard.

nodes.label: ThemeDiscovery (Composer-driven)
nodes.rationale: Merges the tracked themes/ tree with InstalledVersions::getInstalledPackagesByType('liberu-theme'), deduping by realpath so a theme present both ways is one theme; a composition with no themes/ discovers nothing rather than throwing.

nodes.label: Vite inputs are derived, not listed
nodes.rationale: vite.config.js reads every themes/*/theme.json and flattens assets.css and assets.js, so installing a theme package is enough to get it built — and a typo in assets fails the build, which is why an architecture rule checks the files exist.

nodes.label: SetLocale middleware
nodes.rationale: Resolves request param → session → users.locale → Accept-Language → default; precedence request > session > user means a stale session locale can shadow a freshly logged-in user.

nodes.label: LanguageSwitcher (localization-core-livewire)
nodes.rationale: Not mounted anywhere yet.

nodes.label: localization-mymemory adapter
nodes.rationale: Disabled by default; it require-devs localization-core so its suite can boot a real TranslationProviderRegistry while staying free of the implementation at runtime.

nodes.label: Contract packages (analytics-contracts, localization-contracts)
nodes.rationale: Small type: library packages carrying no manifest, used where an adapter needs implementation independence.

nodes.label: Operations stack (Horizon, Octane, Telescope, Pulse)
nodes.rationale: Octane evaluates panel ->colors() once at worker boot, so a colour change needs a worker restart.

nodes.label: Reverb is installed but not wired
nodes.rationale: resources/js/app.js is empty, there is no Echo client and routes/channels.php holds only Laravel's default channel — treat real-time as an available dependency, not a working feature.

nodes.label: Known upgrade blockers
nodes.rationale: spatie/laravel-permission v8 is blocked by filament-shield ~4.x; spiral/roadrunner-http v4 is blocked by laravel/octane ^2.

nodes.label: Per-package PHPStan level ratchet
nodes.rationale: A phpstan-level input per repository set from a measured baseline and raised only; unset is -1 rather than 0 because 0 is a real level. The host analyses app/ only, because a package is honest only when analysed against the tree a consumer installs.

nodes.label: Shared Pint and PHPStan configs via --config
nodes.rationale: PINT.md asks for a pint.json per repository; this deviates because 44 committed copies is how configurations become inconsistent, and Pint has no include mechanism so a shared ruleset is only reachable through --config.

nodes.label: Session handoffs in docs/handoffs/
nodes.rationale: Never in /tmp: WSL's /tmp is wiped on restart and invisible to everyone else, so a handoff written there is lost precisely when the next session needs it.

nodes.label: The host measures the host
nodes.rationale: Coverage <source> is app alone; the Modules and Themes suites were dropped because root autoload-dev maps only Tests\, so they died with 'Class …\Tests\TestCase not found' the moment anything reinstalled.

nodes.label: Module-repo-first source of truth (§3.1)
nodes.rationale: The independent module repository is source of truth; modules/ becomes Composer output and a change made under modules/ survives only until the next composer update.

nodes.label: §6.2 zero-diff gate
nodes.rationale: A clean install must reproduce modules/ and themes/ byte for byte; a diff means someone edited an installed package instead of its repository, and the next install would silently discard the change.

nodes.label: 48-of-48 divergence audit
nodes.rationale: Every package had diverged from its published repo and the monorepo was the side behind; reconciled in favour of upstream through composer update rather than rsync, because Composer is the mechanism the flip moves toward.

nodes.label: Composer vendor stays liberusoftware/ (§3.2)
nodes.rationale: No vendor rename: nothing is republished under a new name, nothing is abandoned, no Packagist vendor permission is needed — and liberu/ was never available, since Packagist protects a vendor once anything publishes under it.

nodes.label: Package naming: -core marks provider-neutrality (§3.3)
nodes.rationale: -core is applied only where a sibling provider adapter ships today, not for 'core of the application'; a provider-shaped contract alone is speculative abstraction.

nodes.label: foundation-filament dissolved
nodes.rationale: An umbrella presenting three independent modules, which §5.6 forbids; its pieces became sessions-devices-filament, module-manager-filament and the host's ThemeColors.

nodes.label: Six out-of-scope packages exiled (§3.4)
nodes.rationale: blog-core, blog-filament, messaging, messaging-api, messaging-filament and search-demo each took their own repository; no foundation package depended on them, which is what made removal a matter of dropping six Composer requires.

nodes.label: Namespace decisions (§3.5)
nodes.rationale: Liberu\Foundation\* and Liberu\Themes\* survive because {Domain} reads as the package family; only Authorization → RolesPermissions and the analytics family actually move.

nodes.label: Discovery and enablement derive from manifests (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: The literal 41-name list plus 3 optional adapters was a second source of truth that could drift.

nodes.label: Architecture rules relocated (12 → 8)
nodes.rationale: A rule lives where it can be acted on; a host failure the host cannot fix is a bad rule. The count landed at 8 rather than the planned 6 because two whole-graph additions were kept.

nodes.label: Package CI: three workflows, not three jobs (§3.9)
nodes.rationale: One tests.yml calling all three reusables queued 176 jobs per 44-repository sweep; split into separate files with install and compatibility on tags plus a concurrency group, one sweep is now 44 jobs.

nodes.label: Per-package coverage ratchet
nodes.rationale: The threshold lives in the package's tests.yml, not phpunit.xml (whose <coverage> element carries no minimum and would be silently ignored) and not a Composer script; two files carrying the same number is two files that can disagree. It ratchets only upward.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: Needed plugin-modifies-install-path and filesystem-based collision detection; a per-run in-memory check missed a directory left by a removed package.

nodes.label: scripts/migrate-testbench
nodes.rationale: Idempotent and takes explicit paths, so it re-runs against checked-out package repositories; it preserves an existing coverage-threshold block, without which one re-run would silently reset every ratchet.

nodes.label: scripts/measure-coverage and set-coverage-thresholds
nodes.rationale: Separate because the second must be re-runnable as coverage grows; a package that lost coverage keeps its old threshold and is reported, because that is a regression to look at rather than a floor to lower.

nodes.label: Migration sequence (steps −1 to 9)
nodes.rationale: Do every cross-cutting change while it is still one atomic commit, so the split is last; step 9 is the point of no return.

nodes.label: Atomic commit does not extend to verification
nodes.rationale: installed.json freezes psr-4 prefixes and package names until a reinstall, so the monorepo can change what a class does and stay green, but not what it is called — the gate for a rename wave is each package's own suite.

nodes.label: ADR exceptions: none (§6)
nodes.rationale: Every case where an exception was available was resolved in favour of a mechanically checkable rule instead.

nodes.label: SearcherRegistry
nodes.rationale: Holds type => callable so searchAll() names nothing; naming post and group was the actual tie to the demo, and an unregistered type is now absent rather than present and empty.

nodes.label: search-demo package
nodes.rationale: Exiled: not a documented capability, default-enabled against §12, and its migrations created unprefixed posts and groups tables.

nodes.label: A package must run against its own dependency tree
nodes.rationale: MessageController::users() selected Jetstream's profile_photo_path and had returned a 500 for four releases in any application without Jetstream, invisible because only a Jetstream-carrying host exercised it.

nodes.label: Code-level conformance audit
nodes.rationale: 37 findings over 122 audited rule clusters; a rule violated in 400 files is one row with a count, not four hundred rows.

nodes.label: Finding ranks and the security flag
nodes.rationale: Four ranks describe realized consequence — breaks a consumer, breaks a promise, unenforced, style only. Security is a flag rather than a fifth rank because a supply-chain exposure is risk, and unenforced is already the risk bucket.

nodes.label: Audit sliced by catching mechanism
nodes.rationale: Classes are Boundary, CI, Arch, Larastan, Pint and Prose; Prose (per-change) is out of scope because an obligation on the next change has no fleet-wide fact behind it and an audit row for one cannot fail.

nodes.label: Livewire aliases are not package-qualified
nodes.rationale: Both -livewire packages register a bare global name, which silently loses to any consumer registering the same alias.

nodes.label: Third-party actions not pinned to commit SHAs
nodes.rationale: 21 references across host and reusable workflows; ranked unenforced with a security flag.

nodes.label: All 44 callers pin the reusable workflow to @main
nodes.rationale: A push to liberusoftware/.github changes every repository's CI instantly with no staging.

nodes.label: declare(strict_types=1) absent almost everywhere
nodes.rationale: 3 of 216 package files and 0 of 5 host files; a sweep is a fleet-wide semantic change, not a formatting one, and declare_strict_types is not in Pint's laravel preset.

nodes.label: Both analytics adapters are inert and nothing says so
nodes.rationale: They register a destination only if a transport is bound, and nothing in the fleet or host binds either — so enabling one sends nothing.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md describes a domain-doc layout that does not exist
nodes.rationale: Neither CONTEXT.md nor docs/adr/ is present, while CONFORMANCE.md §6 resolves exceptions by pointing at ADRs that have no home.

nodes.label: Seven packages call members their declared type does not have
nodes.rationale: jetstream-bridge type-hints Illuminate's base User then calls host-only members through traits it neither requires nor declares; a consumer gets a fatal, not a diagnostic.

nodes.label: Composer basename and installer name lack the module- prefix
nodes.rationale: 8 presentation packages; CONFORMANCE.md §6 states 'ADR exceptions: None' while this exception is in force and undocumented.

nodes.label: Three packages migrate the users table none of them owns
nodes.rationale: profiles, search and identity-socialstream all Schema::table('users'); ordering between them is accidental.

nodes.label: Service-locator prohibition has no rule and is violated
nodes.rationale: 18 app()/resolve() call sites and 30 files importing a Facade in domain source; no stock PHPStan rule catches it.

nodes.label: Three foundation boundaries
nodes.rationale: The application composes, modules own behavior, themes own presentation; dependencies flow through declared capabilities and contracts rather than cross-package implementation classes.

nodes.label: Foundation capability → package matrix
nodes.rationale: Maps the canonical foundation catalog to independently owned packages; product examples are no longer installed here.

nodes.label: Host boundary: /app is composition only
nodes.rationale: Root migrations own only application users and Laravel infrastructure; capability migrations, routes, policies, commands, config, translations and views live with their owning module.

nodes.label: module:validate, theme:validate, foundation:doctor, module:cache
nodes.rationale: Run in CI and during deployment; a validated module cache must be rebuilt when enabled modules, manifests, lockfiles or environment configuration change.

nodes.label: Liberu Real Estate host application
nodes.rationale: The deployable host for a property business, combining independently released domain, API, Filament, Livewire and theme packages while keeping tenancy, teams, authentication and composition in one host.

nodes.label: Portal synchronization modules (Rightmove, Zoopla, OnTheMarket)
nodes.rationale: Independent modules with provider-specific transport contracts.

nodes.label: theme-real-estate-default
nodes.rationale: Extends the Liberu default and base themes through the manifest inheritance chain; selected via THEME_DEFAULT/THEME_PUBLIC.

nodes.label: Real-estate package naming convention
nodes.rationale: Packagist uses liberusoftware/real-estate-*, the independent GitHub sources use liberusoftware/module-real-estate-*, themes use liberusoftware/theme-*.

nodes.label: Admin user-management enhancement
nodes.rationale: Tabbed user form, enriched users table, a read-only view page and three dashboard widgets; backward compatible with no database migrations required.

nodes.label: Admin dashboard widgets
nodes.rationale: UserStatsOverview, LatestUsersWidget and UsersByRoleChart.

nodes.label: lerd local PHP development environment
nodes.rationale: Podman-based and framework-agnostic: every framework is driven by a YAML definition rather than by lerd hardcoding a framework's name.

nodes.label: lerd twelve grouped MCP tools
nodes.rationale: site, service, db, env, runtime, worker, exec, framework, diag, logs, worktree, workspace — each selecting behaviour via an action argument.

nodes.label: Driving optimisation from real traffic
nodes.rationale: Do not read controllers to guess at N+1s: route_timing, then dumps and profiler, then optimize_route joins the symptom to its cause with file:line.

nodes.label: lerd git worktree subdomains
nodes.rationale: Each worktree gets a <branch>.<site>.test subdomain; readiness must come from wait, never from inspecting the tree, because node_modules/ and vendor/ read as finished mid-install.

nodes.label: Laravel Boost guidelines
nodes.rationale: Curated version-specific rules plus the Boost MCP tools; search-docs before code changes because it returns docs matched to installed versions.

nodes.label: Host CI gates
nodes.rationale: composer validate --strict, composer audit --locked, Pint, PHPStan with an explicit memory limit, coverage and Codecov upload on every push and pull request.

nodes.label: Release is a claim about the tree
nodes.rationale: Both halves are checked rather than assumed from a green main run: packages must match their published releases, and the suite must pass against exactly those files. The tag pattern is v-prefixed because an unprefixed pattern matched none of this repository's tags and the workflow had never run.

nodes.label: Container deployment topology
nodes.rationale: One image driven by CONTAINER_MODE — http via Octane/RoadRunner, plus optional reverb and worker profiles — with MySQL, Redis and Mailpit behind health checks.

nodes.label: Sweep AI automation
nodes.rationale: Turns bugs and feature requests into pull requests against main, checking rules such as unit tests for new business logic.

nodes.label: Daily Dependabot updates
nodes.rationale: Composer, npm and github-actions ecosystems at the repository root.

nodes.label: Private Messaging System
nodes.rationale: Direct user-to-user messaging with encrypted bodies, read receipts and policy-based access, delivered as both a Blade/Alpine web UI and a Sanctum-authenticated REST API.

nodes.label: Message Model
nodes.rationale: Holds sender/recipient relations, between()/unread() scopes and markAsRead()/isRead(); keeps conversation querying in one place rather than in controllers.

nodes.label: MessageController
nodes.rationale: Seven actions (index, show, store, markAsRead, destroy, users, unreadCount) that validate input, authorize via policy and handle encryption/decryption at the boundary.

nodes.label: MessagePolicy
nodes.rationale: Laravel Policies chosen over ad-hoc checks: standard pattern, centralized logic, easy to test, and works with Blade directives and middleware. Users view messages they sent or received, update only what they sent, delete either side.

nodes.label: messages table schema
nodes.rationale: sender_id/recipient_id foreign keys with cascade delete, encrypted text body, nullable read_at.

nodes.label: Message encryption at rest
nodes.rationale: Laravel Crypt (AES-256-CBC) encrypts each message body individually. Chosen because it is built in, needs no extra infrastructure, and manages keys via APP_KEY. Per-message rather than per-column encryption allows selective decryption and least privilege. Trade-offs: encrypted messages cannot be searched without decrypting, and key rotation requires re-encrypting everything.

nodes.label: No conversations table
nodes.rationale: Messages are stored directly and conversations derived dynamically: simpler schema, fewer joins, fast direct-message queries. Trade-off: adding group messaging would require refactoring to a conversations table plus a participants pivot.

nodes.label: Conversation query indexes
nodes.rationale: Composite (sender_id, recipient_id) index optimizes the between() scope; a single recipient_id index optimizes unread-message queries used by the conversation list.

nodes.label: Separate API (Sanctum) and web (session) routes
nodes.rationale: Keeps the web UI on session auth while exposing the same behaviour to token clients; enables future mobile app integration without reworking authentication.

nodes.label: Alpine.js for the messaging UI
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Vue/React because it is lightweight, needs no build step for the MVP, integrates with Blade and matches the Livewire ecosystem. Migration to Livewire components is noted as a future option.

nodes.label: Layered authorization
nodes.rationale: Authorization is checked at routes (middleware), controller (policy) and views (Blade directives) so a single missed check cannot bypass access control.

nodes.label: @json() directive for JS contexts
nodes.rationale: Blade's @json() is used instead of raw {{ }} when embedding values into JavaScript, closing an XSS hole found in code review.

nodes.label: Messaging REST API endpoints
nodes.rationale: Seven endpoints: list conversations, conversation with user, send, mark read, delete, list users, unread count.

nodes.label: Messaging web interface
nodes.rationale: Blade views (layout/index/show) with a conversation list, unread counts and a new-message modal.

nodes.label: Messaging test suites
nodes.rationale: MessageTest covers model logic, relationships, scopes and encryption; MessageApiTest covers endpoints, authentication, authorization and validation.

nodes.label: Real-time notification system
nodes.rationale: Dual-channel delivery: every notification is persisted to the database for history and broadcast over websockets for immediacy, so reliability does not depend on the socket connection.

nodes.label: Alternative broadcast services
nodes.rationale: Ably, Laravel Reverb and Soketi are drop-in alternatives to Pusher, so the implementation avoids coupling to one vendor.

nodes.label: Private user broadcast channels
nodes.rationale: App.Models.User.{id}, user.{userId} and notifications.{userId} are all private and require channel authorization, keeping notification payloads off public channels.

nodes.label: Queued notification delivery (ShouldQueue)
nodes.rationale: All notifications implement ShouldQueue so broadcasting and persistence happen off the request cycle.

nodes.label: notifications table
nodes.rationale: UUID primary key for distributed-system compatibility, polymorphic notifiable, JSON data column and read_at tracking.

nodes.label: Laravel Echo client listener
nodes.rationale: Initializes only when Pusher env vars are present, subscribes to the authenticated user channel and re-dispatches a notification-received custom event for the UI to consume.

nodes.label: Advanced search across users, posts and groups
SearchService
nodes.rationale: Service layer holding searchUsers/searchPosts/searchGroups/searchAll so filter-to-query translation is reusable and testable outside controllers.

nodes.label: SearchController
nodes.rationale: Validates filters then delegates to SearchService; validation at the edge prevents malformed queries reaching the database.

nodes.label: Search API endpoints
nodes.rationale: /api/search/users, /posts, /groups and /all, each accepting query, entity filters, date ranges, ordering and per_page (1-100).

nodes.label: Post model
nodes.rationale: belongsTo author, with published/status/byAuthor/dateRange/search scopes.

nodes.label: Group model
nodes.rationale: belongsTo owner, with type/byOwner/search scopes.

nodes.label: Reusable Eloquent search scopes
nodes.rationale: scopeSearch on each model keeps search logic DRY and consistent instead of duplicating LIKE clauses in every controller.

nodes.label: Search database indexes
nodes.rationale: B-tree indexes on searchable and filterable columns (name, title, status, created_at, is_active) plus foreign keys; expected 50-80% reduction in query time on indexed columns.

nodes.label: Full-text indexes
nodes.rationale: Groups carry a full-text index on name/description. Posts deliberately do not: they use plain B-tree indexes and LIKE matching via the search scope.

nodes.label: Search API rate limiting
nodes.rationale: 60 requests per minute per IP protects against DoS and enforces fair resource distribution.

nodes.label: Selective column loading
nodes.rationale: Standalone search controllers select only needed columns (60-90% memory reduction). The shared SearchService does not yet do this and still returns full models.

nodes.label: Enforced pagination limits
nodes.rationale: Default 15, maximum 100 records per page prevents memory exhaustion from unbounded result sets.

nodes.label: modules/search package
nodes.rationale: The search code moved out of app/ into modules/search; the package README is the canonical reference.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/module-search-demo
nodes.rationale: Holds the demo-shaped Post and Group models that the search docs describe.

nodes.label: Full-text search engine migration path
nodes.rationale: LIKE-based search suits small-to-medium datasets; Laravel Scout with Meilisearch/Algolia or Elasticsearch is the documented escape hatch for larger ones.

nodes.label: liberu-module Composer package
nodes.rationale: Modules are independently versioned Composer packages installed into modules/{name}; Composer owns discovery and autoloading.

nodes.label: module.json manifest
nodes.rationale: Owns runtime metadata, provided/required capabilities, enablement defaults and Filament plugin declarations, separate from Composer's installation metadata.

nodes.label: Capability declarations (provides / requires)
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are declared twice on purpose: Composer require controls installation and autoloading, manifest requires/required_capabilities control the enabled runtime graph.

nodes.label: Module categories
nodes.rationale: integration, domain, presentation or theme; framework presentation dependencies must stay out of domain packages.

nodes.label: Explicit module enablement
nodes.rationale: Bundled packages default to disabled in their manifests and the application enables its composition explicitly, so installing a package never implies booting it.

nodes.label: Module manager (provider lifecycle authority)
nodes.rationale: The root application bootstraps only the module manager, which discovers installed liberu-module packages, validates the graph, orders providers by dependency and registers only enabled modules.

nodes.label: No extra.laravel.providers auto-discovery
nodes.rationale: Runtime modules declare their provider in extra.liberu.provider and must not use Laravel's auto-discovery, because the module manager is the single provider lifecycle authority.

nodes.label: module:validate command
nodes.rationale: Checks that Liberu package dependencies are represented consistently, required versions are installed, providers are valid, capability providers are unambiguous and the enabled graph has no gaps or cycles.

nodes.label: No informal cross-module integration
nodes.rationale: A module must not query another module's tables or import its models as an integration API; use a contract, application service, event or documented schema extension instead.

nodes.label: Contract packages
nodes.rationale: Small shared-interface packages let adapters depend on a stable boundary without importing an implementation.

nodes.label: Companion *-filament presentation module
nodes.rationale: Filament code lives in a companion presentation package rather than its domain module, keeping domain packages presentation-agnostic.

nodes.label: filament_plugins manifest declaration
nodes.rationale: The presentation manifest names which panel (admin or app) receives its plugin class; plugin identifiers must be unique within a panel.

nodes.label: App\Filament\ModulePlugins
nodes.rationale: Composes plugin instances from enabled manifests so panel providers never hard-code module plugins.

nodes.label: Admin Filament panel
nodes.rationale: Panel key 'admin' is for operational management surfaces.

nodes.label: App Filament panel
nodes.rationale: Panel key 'app' is for tenant/user-facing functionality.

nodes.label: Package-owned tests
nodes.rationale: Every module carries its own tests under modules/{name}/tests, at minimum metadata tests verifying Composer/manifest agreement, dependencies and the provider.

nodes.label: Reproducible composition from the lockfile
nodes.rationale: Hidden filesystem-scanning conventions are avoided so Composer metadata, the manifest and explicit enablement are enough to reproduce the composition.

nodes.label: Module release workflow
nodes.rationale: Update the changelog, validate the graph, run focused and root suites, release from the package repository, then update the consuming application's constraint and lockfile.

nodes.label: liberu-theme Composer package
nodes.rationale: Themes are independent Composer packages installed into tracked /themes/{name} directories and own presentation only; business rules, authorization, queries and mutations stay in modules.

nodes.label: theme.json manifest
nodes.rationale: Declares name, label, version, provider, type, parent, colors and the declared asset entries.

nodes.label: Theme parent inheritance chain
nodes.rationale: Child themes override only differing assets and inherit views/assets through a finite, validated parent chain; view lookup is child theme, parent chain, module default, then application fallback.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-base
nodes.rationale: Shared root theme: accessible layout, semantic tokens, cascade layers and progressive JS primitives.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-dark
nodes.rationale: Dark presentation achieved purely through token overrides on base.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: Composer 2 plugin handling both liberu-theme and liberu-module: validates kebab-case installer names, rejects unsafe paths and collisions, and installs deterministically to /themes or /modules.

nodes.label: Tracked installed package directories
nodes.rationale: Consuming applications commit both the lockfile and the reproduced /modules and /themes trees; root path repositories let Composer recognize the tracked source at the installer path instead of overwriting it.

nodes.label: Theme selection precedence
nodes.rationale: Tenant-and-surface, then site-and-surface, then configured surface, then safe default. User/session preference may only select a discovered compatible theme; invalid selections warn and fall back.

nodes.label: Semantic design tokens
nodes.rationale: Themes consume tokens for light, dark, contrast, state, focus, motion, spacing, typography, radius, elevation, borders, breakpoints and layering rather than hard-coded values.

nodes.label: Theme accessibility requirements
nodes.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA target verified with automated checks plus keyboard and screen-reader journeys; CSS honors reduced motion, forced colors and bidirectional layout; JS is progressive and CSP-safe.

nodes.label: Deterministic theme builds
nodes.rationale: Builds fail on missing manifest assets or unresolved imports; /public/build is deployment output while source assets remain in each package.

nodes.label: ThemeManager service
nodes.rationale: Discovers themes, resolves the active theme, exposes theme/view/asset paths and registers theme view paths with Laravel's view finder.

nodes.label: ThemeServiceProvider
nodes.rationale: Registers the ThemeManager singleton, determines the active theme at boot, registers theme view paths and Blade directives, and shares theme data with views.

nodes.label: Theme helper functions
nodes.rationale: theme(), active_theme(), set_theme(), theme_asset(), theme_path(), theme_views_path(), theme_layout().

nodes.label: Theme Blade directives
nodes.rationale: @themeCss, @themeJs, @themeAsset, @themeLayout and @themeVite; @themeVite selects declared built entries and falls back to the application bundle when unavailable.

nodes.label: Theme preference persistence
nodes.rationale: Authenticated users persist to users.theme_preference; guests fall back to session storage.

nodes.label: Vite theme asset auto-discovery
nodes.rationale: vite.config.js reads every themes/*/theme.json and builds whatever assets.css and assets.js declare, so a consuming application needs no build change to add a theme.

nodes.label: Unified /themes root directory
nodes.rationale: Theme views, CSS and JS were consolidated from three split resources/ trees into one directory per theme, so a theme is added or removed as a single unit.

nodes.label: Theme release and upgrade flow
nodes.rationale: Release from the theme's own repository, update constraint and lockfile, reinstall, review the tracked /themes diff, validate, build and test. Conflicts are resolved by selecting a package version and reinstalling, never by hand-merging installed output; breaking manifest/token/slot changes need a major version.

nodes.label: Multi-language support
nodes.rationale: English, Spanish, French and German out of the box, with automated machine translation and cached results.

nodes.label: SetLocale middleware
nodes.rationale: Resolution order: locale query parameter, session value, authenticated user's preference, Accept-Language header, then the default locale.

nodes.label: TranslationService (MyMemory)
nodes.rationale: Wraps the free MyMemory API; can be swapped by binding a subclass in a service provider, which keeps callers independent of the translation vendor.

nodes.label: Translation caching
nodes.rationale: API translations are cached for 30 days to stay within MyMemory's free-tier rate limits and avoid repeat calls.

nodes.label: LanguageSwitcher Livewire component
nodes.rationale: Lives in modules/localization-livewire and is mounted where a switcher is wanted.

nodes.label: Localization module split
nodes.rationale: The localization code moved out of app/ into modules/localization, modules/localization-livewire and modules/localization-mymemory; each package README is canonical.

nodes.label: Tabbed user form
nodes.rationale: Basic Info / Roles & Permissions / Account Settings tabs reduce cognitive load on a long form; password is required on create and optional on edit.

nodes.label: Users table filters and badges
nodes.rationale: Role multi-select, email verified, email unverified and recently-joined filters, with role and team count badges for fast visual scanning.

nodes.label: Admin dashboard widgets
nodes.rationale: UserStatsOverview, LatestUsersWidget and UsersByRoleChart give an at-a-glance view of the user base.

nodes.label: Filament Shield role-based access
nodes.rationale: Roles and permissions are managed through Shield on top of Spatie Permission, with team-scoped permissions; no new tables were needed.

nodes.label: Single-context domain docs
nodes.rationale: One root CONTEXT.md glossary and one docs/adr/ directory cover the host plus every modules/ and themes/ package; switch to CONTEXT-MAP.md with per-package contexts only if module vocabularies actually diverge.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md glossary
nodes.rationale: Output naming a domain concept must use the glossary's term; a missing term is a signal of either invented language or a real gap.

nodes.label: docs/adr/ decision records
nodes.rationale: Output contradicting an existing ADR must surface the conflict explicitly rather than silently overriding it.

nodes.label: GitHub Issues as the issue tracker
nodes.rationale: All issue and PRD operations go through the gh CLI, with the repo inferred from git remote.

nodes.label: PRs-as-request-surface flag
nodes.rationale: Currently 'no'. GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare #42 must be resolved by trying gh pr view then gh issue view.

nodes.label: Wayfinder map and child tickets
nodes.rationale: A single wayfinder:map issue holds Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog; child tickets are sub-issues, and blocking uses GitHub's native issue dependencies keyed on the blocker's numeric database id.

nodes.label: Canonical triage labels
nodes.rationale: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix — each label string equals its canonical role name in this repo.

nodes.label: docs/CONFORMANCE.md
nodes.rationale: The conformance deliverable: scope, every decision with its enforcement mechanism, the defect register, and the step -1 to 9 migration sequence with gates and rollback. Later step blocks correct earlier prose in the same document.

nodes.label: Wayfinder map issue #612
nodes.rationale: Closed at 15/15 tickets; its destination was a spec and no production code changed. A fresh effort means a fresh map, not reopening it.

nodes.label: liberusoftware vs liberu vendor prefix
nodes.rationale: The vendor was taken as liberu/* early then reversed by the owner back to liberusoftware/*. This puts the repo in deliberate disagreement with liberusoftware/documentation, which mandates liberu/* — a documentation PR is owed.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/package-testbench
nodes.rationale: Shared test harness every package dev-requires; version 1.2.0 implements all seven boundary rules that were being kept in the host, making their deletion safe.

nodes.label: scripts/migrate-testbench
nodes.rationale: Idempotent fleet migration script, piloted on analytics-core and reverted, moved out of the scratchpad because WSL wipes /tmp on restart.

nodes.label: Packagist namespace registration blocker
nodes.rationale: Nine packages 404 on Packagist, blocking the fleet migration because each package must resolve package-testbench standalone. The fallback is a per-package repositories vcs entry, which unblocks immediately at the cost of a later cleanup release wave.

nodes.label: modules/ is Composer output
nodes.rationale: vendor/composer/installed.json owns the autoload map and is written from each package's published composer.json, so a rename makes the host unbootable until the wave is published. The gate for a rename is each package's own suite, never the host's.

nodes.label: Root composer install clobbers tracked packages
nodes.rationale: A root install reinstalls every package from Packagist over the tracked /modules and /themes files. git checkout alone does not recover it — untracked files the published packages brought in survive and can be committed as if they were real work.

nodes.label: Publishing mirrors all packages, not just changed ones
nodes.rationale: Sweeping only changed packages let three stale packages and one regression reach GitHub; the whole fleet must be swept.

nodes.label: composer.json version fields are load-bearing
nodes.rationale: ModuleValidator compares each manifest against Composer\InstalledVersions, so a bumped manifest fails the boot until the package is published, tagged and composer update'd — expect a red host in between.

nodes.label: A tag whose commit predates a fix
nodes.rationale: Composer resolves the tag, not main, so a stale tag is worse than no tag; bumping and re-tagging closed the gate.

nodes.label: Host architecture boundary rules
nodes.rationale: ModuleBoundariesTest held 15 rules; seven moved to the testbench and the survivors are the whole-graph ones — theme parents resolving, Composer owning every autoload boundary, cross-package namespace dependencies, one Composer vendor, and the two enablement rules.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/.github reusable workflows
nodes.rationale: Three reusable workflows so every repository gets real CI without carrying a copy of the workflow body.

nodes.label: Handoffs live in docs/handoffs/
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md overrides the /handoff skill's temp-directory default because WSL wipes /tmp exactly when the next session needs the document.

nodes.label: Missing config.allow-plugins across packages
nodes.rationale: 0 of 48 packages declared config.allow-plugins, so composer update fails inside every package because pestphp/pest-plugin is blocked; --no-plugins is a measurement workaround, not the fix.

nodes.label: Verify before asserting
nodes.rationale: Several confident claims were wrong on inspection: a CI gate of --min=83 measuring 5.6%, twelve architecture rules of which two never worked, and 'standalone-testable' packages that could not install standalone.

nodes.label: Packagist token stays out of the session
nodes.rationale: The token was never shared or stored; it belongs in ~/.config/composer/auth.json or a GitHub Actions secret, never in a repo or a chat transcript.

nodes.label: Handoff: Conformance Step 5 (Test Redistribution)
nodes.rationale: Written so the next session does not re-derive state: it points at CONFORMANCE.md, the git log and CLAUDE.md rather than restating them, and records only environment state, traps and next steps.

nodes.label: Handoff: Conformance Step 4 (Testbench Migration)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by the step 5 handoff: its blocker is gone and its next-steps are done.

nodes.label: Conformance Step 5 — Test Redistribution
nodes.rationale: Tests move out of the host into the package that owns them; a test belongs in a package only if it needs nothing from the host. Moved so far: settings (3 tests), localization-core (locale middleware), localization-core-livewire (language switcher).

nodes.label: docs/CONFORMANCE.md — Conformance Plan
nodes.rationale: Its "Step N is done" blocks state what was actually found, including where the plan was wrong — the plan is corrected in writing rather than silently.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/package-testbench
nodes.rationale: Shared boundary suites and test bootstrap so a new boundary rule is one testbench release rather than a 44-repository sweep. Version 1.7.0 at the time of this handoff.

nodes.label: Trap: an empty tests/ directory does not publish
nodes.rationale: 34 packages shipped 1.2.0 with no tests/ at all; Pest aborts with 'The test directory [tests] does not exist'. The 44-package sweep passed only because the directory was still on disk locally. Fixed with a tracked tests/.gitkeep. Lesson: a fleet sweep does not prove what the tarball contains — only a reinstall does. Second occurrence of this class of error.

nodes.label: Trap: do not tag before something has run the shipped artifact
nodes.rationale: testbench 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 were tagged with a boundary suite that could not load. A tag is what Packagist publishes, so it is not recoverable the way a push is.

nodes.label: Trap: defineEnvironment() overrides must call parent
nodes.rationale: A package overriding defineEnvironment() without parent::defineEnvironment($app) loses the application key PackageTestCase sets (testbench 1.7.0).

nodes.label: Trap: host goes red between a manifest bump and composer update
nodes.rationale: ModuleValidator compares the manifest against InstalledVersions, so the window between the two is expected red, not a fault.

nodes.label: Trap: WSL DNS drops under parallel Composer
nodes.rationale: Sweep at -P 2 and retry; higher parallelism loses name resolution.

nodes.label: Task #8 — searcher registry in search / search-demo split
nodes.rationale: Moving SearchService::searchPosts()/searchGroups() and two search-api controller actions into search-demo is a three-package refactor, not a move: searchAll() aggregates over types, so the honest design is a searcher registry in `search` that `search-demo` registers into — which is exactly what CONFORMANCE §3.4 objected to being hardcoded. search's own tests follow the code, not the other way round.

nodes.label: Task #9 — adopt preserved messaging and blog tests
nodes.rationale: Tests preserved at commit 33550079 need adopting into their own repositories.

nodes.label: Blocker: theme discovery is not Composer-driven
nodes.rationale: ThemeManager* and ThemeSwitcherTest need installed themes, but discovery reads base_path('themes') rather than InstalledVersions the way ModuleDiscovery does, and Testbench's base path is its own skeleton. Fixing it also closes the theme-support §4 row, where three successive guards had to be loosened to make the package bootable.

nodes.label: Risk: package CI has not been observed green
nodes.rationale: Runs on liberusoftware/module-* queued over an hour; every suite passes locally with the same command CI runs, but nobody has seen the workflows themselves pass since the migration. Check before assuming.

nodes.label: Working agreement: verify before asserting
nodes.rationale: Mutation-test a new rule; outward-facing steps get confirmed; the plan is corrected in writing when wrong; no Claude attribution footers.

nodes.label: liberu-module Composer package type
nodes.rationale: Every module is an independently versioned Composer package of type liberu-module; hosts integrate through declared public boundaries rather than application-specific classes.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: The trusted installer places each package under /modules/<installer-name>. The installed directory stays tracked by the host repository while Composer and its lock file remain the source of version truth.

nodes.label: Installation does not imply enablement
nodes.rationale: Installing a package implies neither runtime enablement nor commercial entitlement; enablement is a separate explicit decision driven by the manifest's default_enabled.

nodes.label: Liberu security disclosure policy
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities go to security@liberusoftware.com with reproduction details and affected version, never through public GitHub issues, so the report can be handled privately.

nodes.label: Capability boundary discipline
nodes.rationale: Consumers grant only the permissions needed for exported capabilities and must not couple to internal tables or classes; authorization stays the host's responsibility unless a public authorizer contract is published.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/module-manager
nodes.rationale: The near-universal dependency of foundation modules — it discovers manifests and resolves enablement order.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/analytics-contracts
nodes.rationale: A contract package lets analytics adapters stay independent of the core implementation and of each other.

nodes.label: Liberu Activity and Comments
nodes.rationale: Owns generic authorized activity timelines, mentions, subscriptions, internal comments, attachments and visibility controls as one versioned package. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\ActivityComments\ActivityCommentsServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

nodes.label: Contract: ActivityAuthorizer
nodes.rationale: A published authorizer contract is what moves authorization responsibility from the host into the package boundary.

nodes.label: Liberu Analytics Core
nodes.rationale: Versioned event envelopes, consent, mapping, minimization, routing, deduplication, queues, redaction and delivery audit. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Analytics\Core\AnalyticsServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

nodes.label: Liberu Google Analytics
nodes.rationale: Consent-aware Google event mapping, property/stream configuration, validation, ecommerce parameters and diagnostics. Category adapter, provider Liberu\Analytics\Google\AnalyticsGoogleServiceProvider, default_enabled no — it needs third-party credentials so it ships installed but off.

nodes.label: Liberu Meta Server-Side Tracking
nodes.rationale: Consent-aware Meta event mapping, browser/server deduplication, normalization/hashing, protected configuration and diagnostics. Category adapter, provider Liberu\Analytics\Meta\AnalyticsMetaServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

nodes.label: Liberu API Access
nodes.rationale: Token and service-identity policy, scopes, versions, rate limits, idempotency, expiry and revocation. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\ApiAccess\ApiAccessServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Owns personal_access_tokens, api_idempotency_keys and api_service_identities.

nodes.label: API module index
nodes.rationale: Each API package is a thin versioned transport adapter over exactly one core package, enforcing authentication, team context, validation, authorization, pagination, bounded input and documented response contracts — so transport concerns never leak into the domain.

nodes.label: Core module index
nodes.rationale: Core packages own domain rules, application actions, policies, persistence, events, jobs, contracts, retention and tests, and never depend on API, Filament, Livewire, themes or the host's App classes.

nodes.label: Filament module index
nodes.rationale: Filament 5 packages provide panel resources and workflows over one matching core package; they do not own domain invariants or persistence.

nodes.label: Feature module index
nodes.rationale: Feature specifications are framework-neutral and map one-to-one to core packages and their optional API, Filament and Livewire adapters. React, Vue, Nuxt, React Native and Flutter indexes are deliberately deferred and not generated by this refactor.

nodes.label: Real Estate project scope
nodes.rationale: The scope the application currently selects; its authoritative product plan is projects/real-estate/REAL-ESTATE.md.

nodes.label: One core package per adapter
nodes.rationale: Every API, Filament and Livewire package adapts exactly one core package, which is what keeps the presentation and transport layers substitutable and the domain layer dependency-free.

nodes.label: Liberu Application Core
nodes.rationale: Application metadata, health/readiness, secure response defaults, clocks and shared identifiers. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\ApplicationCore\ApplicationCoreServiceProvider, default_enabled no, owns no migration.

nodes.label: Contract: Clock
nodes.rationale: An injectable clock is what makes time-dependent domain rules testable without freezing global state.

nodes.label: Liberu Audit
nodes.rationale: Actor, tenant, request and correlation-aware material-change audit with export and retention boundaries. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\Audit\AuditServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Owns activity_log plus a tamper-evidence migration.

nodes.label: Liberu Currency Context
nodes.rationale: ISO metadata, precise money values, currency roles, formatting and effective-dated exchange-rate contracts. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\Currency\CurrencyServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

nodes.label: Contract: ExchangeRateProvider
nodes.rationale: Rates are effective-dated and supplied through a contract so the package never carries a rate source of its own.

nodes.label: Liberu Developer Experience
nodes.rationale: Local environment, fixtures, quality scripts, CI, architecture checks, documentation and upgrade diagnostics. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\DeveloperExperience\DeveloperExperienceServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

nodes.label: FoundationDoctorCommand
nodes.rationale: The only console command published by any module in this chunk — upgrade and environment diagnostics.

nodes.label: Liberu Feature Flags
nodes.rationale: Typed flags, environment/tenant/actor targeting, stable rollout, ownership, expiry and telemetry boundaries. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\FeatureFlags\FeatureFlagsServiceProvider, default_enabled no.

nodes.label: Liberu Files and Media
nodes.rationale: Secure storage contracts, uploads, validation, scanning, metadata, transformations, access and retention. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\Files\FilesMediaServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Owns the media table.

nodes.label: Contract: MalwareScanner
nodes.rationale: Scanning is a contract, not an implementation, so the package ships no bundled scanner engine.

nodes.label: Liberu Identity Administration (identity-filament)
nodes.rationale: Optional Filament user and role administration surface. Category presentation, provider Liberu\Foundation\IdentityFilament\IdentityFilamentServiceProvider, default_enabled no, owns no migration — presentation packages hold no persistence. Note the installed directory here is modules/identity-core-filament while the installer name declared in the README is identity-filament.

nodes.label: Liberu Identity
nodes.rationale: Provider-neutral authentication policy, identifier normalization and security events. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\Identity\IdentityServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Owns the passkeys table. Note the installed directory is modules/identity-core while the declared installer name is identity.

nodes.label: IdentityEvent
nodes.rationale: The only package-owned event class published by any module in this chunk.

nodes.label: passkeys table migration
nodes.rationale: Passkey persistence lives in the identity module rather than the host, even though the host's User uses no passkey trait.

nodes.label: Liberu Social Identity
nodes.rationale: Social provider redirects, callbacks, identity linking, protected credentials and account synchronization. Category adapter, provider Liberu\Foundation\Identity\Socialstream\Providers\SocialstreamServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Makes users.password nullable and owns connected_accounts.

nodes.label: Contract: ConnectedAccountOwner
nodes.rationale: One of the seven contracts the host's User model implements, which is how the host opts into social identity without the module knowing App\Models\User.

nodes.label: Liberu Import and Export
nodes.rationale: Schemas, mapping, dry runs, validation, queued execution, progress, error reports, authorization and retention. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\ImportExport\ImportExportServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Owns data_transfers.

nodes.label: Liberu Integrations
nodes.rationale: Provider credentials, adapter capabilities, OAuth boundaries, rotation, connection tests, sync and reconciliation. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\Integrations\IntegrationsServiceProvider, default_enabled no. Owns integration_connections and is the shared credential substrate every third-party adapter builds on.

nodes.label: Liberu Jetstream Bridge
nodes.rationale: Fortify and Jetstream-compatible registration, profile, password, team and account-deletion actions. Category foundation, provider Liberu\Foundation\JetstreamBridge\Providers\FortifyServiceProvider, default_enabled no, owns no migration — it bridges to first-party Laravel auth packages rather than reimplementing them.

nodes.label: Livewire Module Index
nodes.rationale: Livewire 4 packages provide interactive state and views over exactly one matching core package; they validate and authorize at the boundary and delegate mutations rather than owning them.

nodes.label: Liberu MyMemory Translation
nodes.rationale: Ships as an optional cached adapter in the `adapter` category so the host can add machine translation without the core localization package depending on a third-party service.

nodes.label: Liberu Module Manager
nodes.rationale: Owns manifest discovery, dependency resolution, deployment enablement, registry caching and diagnostics for the whole composition, so enablement is a decision the manager resolves rather than a side effect of Composer install.

nodes.label: Real Estate Core
nodes.rationale: Owns the real-estate operational boundaries the shared organizations module does not own - team-scoped branches and stable branch codes - and stays presentation-neutral, passing explicit team context at every mutation boundary.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: A trusted Composer installer places each package under /modules/<installer-name>. The installed directory stays tracked by the host repository while Composer and its lock file remain the source of version truth.

nodes.label: Installation Does Not Imply Enablement
nodes.rationale: Every module README states that installation implies neither runtime enablement nor commercial entitlement, so adding a package to the composition is a separate decision from booting it.

nodes.label: Enabled By Default Declaration
nodes.rationale: All ten templated module READMEs in this chunk declare `Enabled by default: no`, including foundation packages such as module-manager, localization, notifications, observability, organizations-teams and profiles. The host CLAUDE.md instead states 37 of 40 manifests set default_enabled true, so README and manifest may disagree - flagged for review.

nodes.label: Capability Declaration
nodes.rationale: Each package exports named capabilities (e.g. foundation.modules, identity.profiles) that hosts and dependent modules bind to, instead of coupling to application-specific classes.

nodes.label: Manifest Service Provider
nodes.rationale: Each manifest names one service provider class under the Liberu\Foundation namespace; the host registers it explicitly rather than through extra.laravel.providers auto-discovery.

nodes.label: Declared Public Boundary
nodes.rationale: Hosts integrate a package through its declared provider, capabilities and published contracts; consumers must not couple to internal tables or classes, and authorization stays the host's responsibility unless a public authorizer contract is published.

nodes.label: Standalone Package Test Suite
nodes.rationale: Every package ships its own tests, run from a compatible host checkout as `vendor/bin/pest modules/<name>/tests`; changes must preserve the manifest, provider integration, package boundaries and declared PHP/Laravel compatibility.

nodes.label: Team-Scoped Boundary
nodes.rationale: Real-estate transports and domain records are scoped to a team and pass explicit team context at every mutation boundary; unauthorized cross-team access surfaces as 403 Forbidden rather than a silently filtered result.

nodes.label: Presentation-Neutral Core Package
nodes.rationale: A domain core package owns rules and persistence but no UI, so Filament, Livewire and API adapters can be added, swapped or omitted without touching domain behaviour.

nodes.label: Adapter Over One Matching Core Package
nodes.rationale: Each -api, -filament and -livewire package adapts exactly one matching core package: it validates and authorizes at the boundary and delegates mutations to the core rather than reimplementing them.

nodes.label: Unprefixed Composer Name vs module- GitHub Repository
nodes.rationale: The published Composer/Packagist name drops the `module-` prefix carried by the GitHub source repository, so liberusoftware/real-estate-instructions on Composer is module-real-estate-instructions on GitHub.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key Header
nodes.rationale: Replays a completed mutation for the same team, key and request body (8-255 chars), so a retried POST/PATCH/DELETE cannot double-apply; a mismatch returns 409 Conflict.

nodes.label: 429 RateLimited Response
nodes.rationale: Every instructions operation declares a 429 response carrying a Retry-After header, making rate limiting part of the published contract rather than an undocumented gateway behaviour.

nodes.label: Instruction Record
nodes.rationale: Team-scoped agency instruction covering agreements, ownership checks, terms, disclosures, approvals and withdrawal.

nodes.label: Instruction Status Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: draft, pending_approval, approved, withdrawn, rejected - with approved_at and withdrawn_at timestamps; delete archives rather than destroys (204 Instruction archived).

nodes.label: Letting Lifecycle Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Applications, referencing, deposits, agreements, move-in/out, renewals, rent changes and notices, each an explicit lifecycle capability on a team-scoped letting record.

nodes.label: Archive Instead of Destroy on DELETE
nodes.rationale: DELETE returns 204 with the description 'archived' for branches, agencies, territories and instructions, so the transport contract never promises hard deletion.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/localization-contracts
nodes.rationale: A separate contracts package lets localization-mymemory adapt a third-party translation service while the core localization package depends only on the contract, keeping the adapter's implementation independent.

nodes.label: ObservabilityActor Contract
nodes.rationale: Published so the host User model can gate Telescope and Pulse dashboards without the observability module knowing about App\Models\User.

nodes.label: Shared users Table Extension
nodes.rationale: Profiles adds locale, theme_preference and timezone columns to the host-owned users table via three migrations - the users table is the one table no package owns.

nodes.label: Teams, Membership and Invitation Tables
nodes.rationale: teams, team_user and team_invitations plus a 2026 hardening migration; these tables are the substrate the whole composition's tenant scoping resolves against.

nodes.label: module:features Console Command
nodes.rationale: Lists or searches feature declarations across installed modules, making the fleet's declared features queryable from one place.

nodes.label: Real Estate Listings
nodes.rationale: Team-scoped listing records covering channel content, pricing, availability, publication rules, portal feeds and reconciliation. Domain package stays presentation-agnostic; UI and API live in companion -filament/-livewire/-api packages.

nodes.label: Real Estate Listings API
nodes.rationale: Team-scoped API adapter for listings, kept separate from the domain package so the domain carries no HTTP concerns.

nodes.label: Real Estate Marketing
nodes.rationale: Provider-neutral, team-scoped campaign planning and delivery metadata for listings and properties. External providers belong in replaceable adapters so the domain never depends on a specific vendor.

nodes.label: OpenAPI v1 — Real Estate Marketing
nodes.rationale: Delete is documented as 204 'Archived' rather than a hard delete, so campaign history survives removal.

nodes.label: Real Estate Matching
nodes.rationale: Team-scoped applicant requirements, affordability, preferences, scoring, alerts, feedback and exclusions.

nodes.label: Real Estate Media and Documents
nodes.rationale: Provider-neutral media and document records for photos, floorplans, video, certificates, brochures, rights, ordering and retention. Neutrality keeps storage/CDN vendors out of the domain package.

nodes.label: Real Estate Media and Documents API
nodes.rationale: Explicitly described as the versioned team-scoped API adapter for the Composer package liberusoftware/real-estate-media-and-documents.

nodes.label: Real Estate Media and Documents Filament
Real Estate Media and Documents Livewire
OpenAPI v1 — Real Estate Media and Documents
Real Estate Offers
nodes.rationale: Domain package the offers API adapter fronts; referenced from this chunk only through its adapter, its own README is not in this chunk.

nodes.label: OpenAPI v1 — Real Estate Offers
nodes.rationale: The only spec in this chunk beyond plain CRUD: it adds status transition, proof and timeline operations, because an offer is a negotiation with an auditable decision history rather than a record you merely edit.

nodes.label: Offer Transition, Proof and Timeline Operations
nodes.rationale: POST /offers/{id}/transition/{status}, POST /offers/{id}/proof and GET /offers/{id}/timeline model the offer lifecycle as explicit state changes with recorded evidence, instead of letting a PATCH silently move an offer between statuses.

nodes.label: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme
nodes.rationale: Every real-estate v1 spec declares a single global `security: [{sanctum: []}]` with an http/bearer scheme named Sanctum, so no endpoint in the fleet is unauthenticated by omission.

nodes.label: Shared PaginationMeta Schema
nodes.rationale: Identical `{current_page, per_page, total, last_page}` object in every spec, so list responses paginate the same way across modules.

nodes.label: Composer Unprefixed / GitHub module- Prefix

nodes.label: Provider-Neutral Domain, Replaceable Adapters

nodes.label: Unprefixed Composer Name vs module- GitHub Repo
nodes.rationale: The Composer/Packagist package name drops the module- prefix that the GitHub source repository carries, so the same package is addressed by two different names depending on which system is naming it.

nodes.label: No App\ Namespace Dependency

nodes.label: Migration Owns Only the Package's Tables
nodes.rationale: A module's migration creates only the tables that package owns, and disabling the module does not delete data — enablement is a boot decision, not a data lifecycle decision.

nodes.label: Immutable Property History Entries
nodes.rationale: Property changes are recorded as immutable history entries rather than in-place edits, preserving an audit trail of lifecycle status changes.

nodes.label: Replaceable Integration Services
nodes.rationale: Provider credentials and transport live in replaceable integration services outside the sync core, so a portal provider can be swapped without touching domain records.

nodes.label: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme

nodes.label: Shared Error Schema

nodes.label: Shared PaginationMeta Schema

nodes.label: OpenAPI 3.1.0 Versioned API Contract

nodes.rationale: Rightmove and sales-progression DELETE endpoints return 204 described as 'Archived', preserving records rather than destroying them; the valuations and viewings specs describe the same verb as 'Deleted', so the convention is not uniform across the fleet.

nodes.label: Valuation Workflow Transitions

nodes.label: Viewing Lifecycle Transitions
nodes.rationale: Viewing state changes are POST sub-resources (confirm, complete, cancel, no-show) rather than PATCH field writes, making each lifecycle move a distinct named operation.

nodes.label: Rightmove Sync Operation

nodes.label: Capability Boundary Integration
nodes.rationale: Hosts integrate a package through its declared capabilities and public contracts rather than application-specific classes; consumers must not couple to internal tables or classes.

nodes.rationale: Shared panel and interactive adapters are supplied by the foundation packages while product resources and components stay under their owning project scope, keeping product features out of the shared foundation.

nodes.label: Replaceable provider credentials and transport
nodes.rationale: Credentials and transport implementations stay behind a replaceable boundary so swapping a provider's HTTP client or account never reaches the domain.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/boilerplate-scripts
nodes.rationale: Release and maintenance automation is generic and shipped as a dev dependency rather than copied per meta repository, so every Composer-based meta repo whose modules and themes live in independent GitHub repositories runs the same tooling.

nodes.label: .liberu-meta.json meta-repository config
nodes.rationale: One copied-and-customized config carries organization, genre, repository, component paths, prefixes and extra Composer packages, so the scripts stay generic.

nodes.rationale: Performs a repeatable local or production install without destructive migrations.

nodes.label: update.sh
nodes.rationale: Updates dependencies and validates the project; --release 1.2.3 only commits, tags, pushes and creates the GitHub release after the checks succeed.

nodes.label: scripts/fleet
nodes.rationale: Fans a command across the component repositories once those repositories are the source of truth. tag is deliberately separate and only ever acts on an explicit --only list, because a tag is what gets published while a push is recoverable.

nodes.label: publish-components (removed)
nodes.rationale: Rsynced a monorepo into its component repositories — the opposite direction, and meaningless once those repositories are the source of truth. Replaced by fleet.

nodes.label: set-coverage-thresholds
nodes.rationale: Writes each measured figure into the package's tests.yml, ratcheting only upward — a package that has lost coverage keeps its threshold and is reported rather than silently lowered.

nodes.label: measure-coverage
nodes.rationale: Resolves each package from nothing and runs its own suite under pcov, so the figure is evidence from a standalone resolution rather than the host's.

nodes.label: measure-phpstan
nodes.rationale: Finds the highest level each package's src/ passes by bisection over a standalone resolution; levels are monotone, so four runs settle it instead of eleven.

nodes.label: set-phpstan-levels
nodes.rationale: Writes each measured level into tests.yml as the reusable workflow's phpstan-level input, ratcheting only upward and preserving the existing coverage-threshold.

nodes.label: Upward-only quality ratchet
nodes.rationale: Both coverage thresholds and PHPStan levels are per-package figures that only ever rise; a regression is reported instead of relaxing the gate.

nodes.label: Non-interactive, fail-on-error commands
nodes.rationale: All commands are non-interactive and fail on errors so they can run unattended in CI.

nodes.label: Packagist credentials from the environment
nodes.rationale: PACKAGIST_USERNAME and PACKAGIST_API_TOKEN are read from the environment and must never be committed; GitHub operations require an authenticated gh CLI.

nodes.label: Component repositories are the source of truth
nodes.rationale: Modules, themes and shared tooling live in independent GitHub repositories; the meta repository is Composer output, which is what makes a monorepo-to-package sync meaningless and a fan-out runner correct.

nodes.label: theme.json manifest
nodes.rationale: The manifest is the single declared surface for name, type, parent and asset entry points; it is the only asset entry-point index, so build inputs are derived from it rather than listed twice.

nodes.label: Theme parent inheritance chain
nodes.rationale: A public theme declares base as its parent and resolves missing views and assets up the chain, so only the shared root has to ship every layout.

nodes.label: Presentation-only package boundary
nodes.rationale: A theme carries no domain behaviour — that stays in modules — and the host keeps control of theme selection and fallback, so a theme can never become a place where business rules hide.

nodes.label: Safe theme fallback
nodes.rationale: Hosts must retain a working base/default theme so that an unavailable optional asset or capability degrades instead of breaking the page.

nodes.label: Theme accessibility baseline
nodes.rationale: Keyboard access, visible focus, semantic landmarks, readable contrast, reduced motion, zoom/reflow and system-font fallbacks are required of every theme, not optional polish.

nodes.label: Host Vite build of theme entry points
nodes.rationale: vite.config.js derives its inputs from themes/*/theme.json, so installing a theme is enough to get it built — and a directory rename changes the input set, requiring a rebuild.

nodes.label: No bundled third-party assets without provenance
nodes.rationale: Themes ship their own sources only; any font, image, icon, video or template added later must carry its licence and attribution.

nodes.label: Theme testing expectations
nodes.rationale: Manifest parsing, provider registration, production asset compilation, supported host surfaces, responsive layout, keyboard navigation, contrast and fallback are all validated, and visual changes carry before/after evidence.

nodes.label: Unpublished theme preview image
nodes.rationale: No maintained preview is published yet; one must be added under .github/assets/ before claiming visual-regression coverage.

nodes.label: Private security disclosure (security@liberusoftware.com)
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities must not be reported through public issues.

nodes.label: base theme (Liberu Base)
nodes.rationale: Shared semantic tokens, accessible layout and progressive presentation primitives live at the shared root so every public theme inherits one accessible baseline.

nodes.label: default theme (Liberu Default)
nodes.rationale: Neutral public and portal defaults built on Liberu Base.

nodes.label: dark theme (Liberu Dark)
nodes.rationale: Dark, reduced-glare presentation with a system fallback.

nodes.label: clear-signal theme (Clear Signal)
nodes.rationale: Teal signal on a quiet neutral workbench.

nodes.label: real-estate-default theme
nodes.rationale: Presentation only: it composes the default and base parents, owns real-estate visual identity and view composition, and never queries module tables, replaces policies or implements domain workflows.

nodes.label: Declared supported host surfaces
nodes.rationale: A theme names the host surfaces it supports (application.shell, identity.auth, foundation.account, blog.index) so a host can tell before installing which screens it actually covers.

nodes.label: Theme rename: liberu-base becomes base (2.0)
nodes.rationale: standards/THEMES.md derives both the repository name and the install path from one {name}, and this theme carried three different ones. A theme's name is a stable manifest surface, so making the manifest agree with the unchanged Composer package name is a major release.

nodes.label: standards/THEMES.md
nodes.rationale: Derives repository name and install path from a single {name}, which is why three divergent names counted as a defect.

nodes.label: ThemeDiscovery realpath dedupe
nodes.rationale: Discovery merges the tracked tree with Composer's installed theme packages and dedupes by realpath — so mid-wave a stale themes/liberu-base and a fresh themes/base do not dedupe and two themes appear until the stale directory is removed.

nodes.label: Child-theme relative CSS import across install dirs
nodes.rationale: A child theme importing the shared root by path crosses the install directory, so a rename of the parent directory moves the import path with it.

nodes.label: Real-estate theme extension points

nodes.label: Semantic design tokens (Tailwind v4 + CSS custom properties)
nodes.rationale: Components consume semantic tokens rather than hard-coded brand values, so canvas, surface, text, focus, state, typography, spacing, motion and layering can be re-themed without touching components.

nodes.label: Asset budgets: 80 KiB CSS / 40 KiB JS compressed
nodes.rationale: The manifest is the only asset entry-point index and generated output is not committed; the budget keeps the built theme small enough for a portal front end.

nodes.label: Semantic versioning over tokens, slots, view names, entry points

nodes.label: Do not edit installed files under themes/
nodes.rationale: Installed theme directories are Composer output; a local edit is overwritten by the next update, so selection goes through the manifest and THEME_* host configuration.
